column5: The statement confirms the course's date (20/04/1964) and the closing sentence of the dock speech, the 8,500 Defiance Campaign volunteers, the 1956 arrest of 156 leaders for treason (acquitted on all counts about five years later), that the ANC was formed in 1912 and kept to constitutional means until 1949, Mandela's arrest in Natal on 5 August 1962 (so Welsh's date for the 27-year count is Mandela's own), and the official 69 Africans killed at Sharpeville, stated by Mandela in 1964 as a contemporaneous figure.

Mandela says Umkhonto was formed in November 1961 and had its first operation on 16/12/1961, when the Manifesto was issued and government buildings in Johannesburg, Port Elizabeth and Durban were attacked. The course (Module 5 lesson 2) says the ANC 'formed an armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe, on 16/12/1961'. Say: Umkhonto was formed in 11/1961 and announced itself with attacks and a Manifesto on 16/12/1961. He also says the ANC itself stayed non-violent and only agreed not to discipline members who took part in 'properly controlled violence'.

column4: the case for sabotage and its limits
column5: Mandela describes four forms of violence (sabotage, guerrilla war, terrorism, open revolution) and says MK chose the first, aimed at the economy and symbols of apartheid with orders not to kill or injure. He denies the ANC is communist, says he never joined the Communist Party but was named under the Suppression of Communism Act, that the Freedom Charter is no blueprint for a socialist state but calls for nationalisation of mines, banks and monopoly industry, and that he admires British and US institutions. Use for Module 5 lesson 5: a defendant's prepared case, partisan and self-protective, and the course's own limit 'a prepared statement by one party' is right.

column4: figures he cites on poverty and education
column5: Mandela quotes: Africans about 70 per cent of the population in the 1960 republic referendum from which they were excluded; per-head state spending in 1960 to 1961 of 12.46 rand on African pupils against 144.57 rand on white pupils in the Cape; only 5,660 African children passing the Junior Certificate and 362 matric in 1962; about 40 per cent of African children aged 7 to 14 out of school; a Johannesburg poverty datum line of 42.84 rand a month against an average wage of 32.24 rand, with 46 per cent of African families below it; 58,491 new tuberculosis cases in 1961. These are his figures, quoted from officials and the Institute of Race Relations in 1964; they differ from Welsh's per-pupil figures (1953 and 1969 to 1970), so do not mix years.

column4: earlier massacres and his Africa tour
column5: He lists earlier killings of Africans by police and white civilians: 24 at Port Elizabeth in 1920, more than 100 at Bulhoek in 1921, and over 200 in South-West Africa in a dog-tax rising, which he dates 1924 (the Bondelswarts rising is usually dated 1922 [check]). The last item links Module 5 to Module 2's South West Africa. He also lists the 1962 supporters he met on his African tour (Nyerere, Haile Selassie, Ben Bella, Keita, Senghor, Sekou Toure, Tubman, Obote), a primary link to Modules 3 and 4.
